title: Enterprise priority sprint-slot syndication and decommitment policy
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Define a productized process and lightweight tooling for allocating scarce engineering sprint slots to top accounts (VIPs) and formalizing decommitment / partial-delivery policies. Goal is to reduce negotiation friction, improve predictability for customers and engineering teams, and create measurable SLAs and credit/compensation mechanics when commitments change.

Why now: Several enterprise renewals and active escalations in the last 6 months have derived directly from unclear expectations about delivery timing. We currently react with ad hoc promises that create churn across squads and risk on-quarter delivery targets. This initiative aims to create a repeatable guarded process that scales as Dedicated/Private customers grow.

Scope (in-scope):
- Policy and decision flow for allocating named sprint slots to VIP feature work across multiple squads (syndication model).
- Lightweight public-facing commitment ledger (readable by customer PMs) showing assigned slot, acceptance criteria, buffer, and ownership.
- Decommitment policy: thresholds for automatic escalation, crediting rules, and staged mitigation (partial features, phased rollouts, paid accelerators).
- Operational playbook for PMs/SEs: intake checklist, acceptance criteria, QA gating, and fallbacks.
- Dashboarding for SLAs: response time to acknowledgement, time-to-delivery variance, % of commitments met.

Out of scope: changes to core billing model, legal contract rewrites beyond template addenda, major infra changes to Dedicated runtime.

Success metrics (first 3 months post-rollout):
- Target: Reduce VIP negotiation cycles by 40% (measured by number of triage meetings per request).
- >85% of assigned sprint slots have defined acceptance criteria and a delivery buffer at time of assignment.
- Decommitment events trigger pre-defined compensations (credits or priority credits) in 100% of identified cases per policy.

Approach and design decisions:
1) Syndication broker: implement a light "slot broker" owned by product ops that can assign fractional sprint commitments across squads (e.g., Slot #A: 2 dev-weeks from Squad Alpha, 1 dev-week from Squad Beta). This avoids hard reassignments and reduces scope creep.
2) Buffering: mandate a default 20% capacity buffer on all VIP slots to absorb minor regressions. Teams can reduce buffer by mutual agreement with written acceptance.
3) Commitment ledger: single-page read-only Confluence plus an API endpoint for account PMs to retrieve slot status. Ledger rows include slot id, feature summary, criteria, owners, buffer, expected delivery sprint, and fallback.
4) Decommitment tiers: "Minor delay" (<2 sprints) => automated credit of advisory hours + prioritized patch lane; "Major delay" (>=2 sprints) => credit against next quarter reserved capacity or agreed product credit. Tiers chosen to balance customer trust and internal predictability.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict SLAs (monetary penalties) would reduce ambiguity but increase legal friction; opted for credits and priority mechanisms to maintain velocity while giving customers tangible remediation.
- A heavy-weight booking UI would provide clarity but increase build cost; we will iterate from Confluence + simple API and invest in UI only after 2 quarters of telemetry.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1-2: Finalize policy doc + Confluence ledger template (PM & Eng review).
- Week 3: Launch pilot with 3 strategic enterprise customers (one on Dedicated, two on Hosted).
- Week 6: Collect telemetry and iterate policy; incorporate ENG feedback on operational load.
- Week 10: Gradual GA to accounts with renewal horizon within 6 months.

Monitoring and alerts:
- Dashboard: % slots with acceptance criteria, slot reassignments per sprint, time between assignment and acknowledgement.
- Alert: any slot decommitment not handled within 48 hours escalates to VP Product and Solutions Engineering.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket (definition of done):
- Policy doc published with sign-off from Legal, Sales Ops, Solutions Eng, and VP Product.
- Confluence ledger template created and seeded with pilot slots.
- Small API endpoint (internal) to fetch slot metadata (health check + read-only access for customer PMs).
- Pilot with 3 accounts executed and retrospective notes captured.

Open questions:
- Do we need to add a financial SLA option for customers with contract power? (Legal input needed)
- Will Dedicated customers expect a stronger contractual credit (TBD by Sales/Legal)?
- How will this integrate with existing renewal/discount workflows?

Next steps (owners):
- PM (Maya): finalize policy and coordinate Legal sign-off (due 2026-02-22).
- Eng (Rishi): prototype internal API + ledger seed scripts (due 2026-03-01).
- Solutions Eng (Lina Ortiz): identify pilot customers and prepare kickoff decks (due 2026-02-28).
- Design (Emilie Park): minimal ledger UX + email template for customers (due 2026-02-26).
